When you want to talk about results and time, you can use a Perfect - ing form. You use this type of structure when you want to emphasize that one thing happens before another. It can have the same meaning as because.
Having published a lot of children's books, I know how crucial the first reviews are.
In this case, the action that comes first is Having published a lot of books. It is clear that the action I know how crucial the first reviews are comes next.
The meaning is: I know how crucial the first reviews are because I have published a lot of books.

Report Verbs with Impersonal Passive Construction
When you want to report a fact or belief, you can use a variety of ways to construct your ideas. When you do not want to mention the source of the information, you can use a passive structure.

You can use the structure It + passive verb + that + finite clause.
A finite clause contain a verb which shows tense.

For example:
It was reported that the army was crossing the frontier.
It has been shown that the theory is correct.
It is proposed that prices should increase next year.

The following are report verbs you can use: admit, declare, hope propose, show, agree, discover, intend, prove, state, allege, establish, know, recommend, suggest, announce, estimate, mention, regret, suppose, assume, expect, notice report, think, believe, explain, object, request, understand, claim, fear, observe, reveal, consider, feel, presume, say, discover, find, promise and see.

Boris: Hi Denise.
Denise: Oh, hi Boris. So, what do you think? The launch is going very well don't you think?
Boris: Yes, it seems to be. It's agreed that this is the best location for this type of launch. I really like the set-up with the kids on the floor in front of Marisa.
Denise: Yes, it was decided that it was better to make the focus about the kids even though we need to sell the book to the parents. It was assumed that if the kids were engrossed in the parts that Marisa reads, then the parents will buy the book.

Boris: That makes sense. Denise, have you read any reviews of the book yet? I'm curious to know what the initial reaction is.
Denise: Yes, anticipating a good response, I read a review that I saw on a blog this morning. I gave an advance copy to a friend of mine because she has kids. Knowing of her concern for her kids' safety on the internet, I knew she would be interested in the book. It wasn't understood that she would review it but she did and she loved it.

Boris: So it was favorable? Having published a lot of children's books, I know how crucial the first reviews are.
Denise: Yes, she liked the concept and the story. She really enjoyed the illustrations. Having so many options for illustrators, it was hard to choose the best one for this book. My friend called the illustrations breath-taking. That's high praise! She also recommended that readers put in orders with us now. That will create even more buzz before we even release the book. It's known that pre-release hype is the best way to increase sales, so I'm really pleased that she added this to her review.
Boris: Yes. Having seen first-hand how valuable that hype can be, I'm really pleased with this review, too.
